svg.aria-label: Normal-chest-radiograph triage as an operating-point problem, using the 2026 UK silent trial. 63,083 chest radiographs from five NHS sites over 12 months. The AI called 50,661 (80 percent) abnormal and 12,422 (20 percent) normal. Sensitivity 97 percent, specificity 35 percent, positive predictive value 57 percent, negative predictive value 94 percent. AI and radiologist agreed the study was normal for 18.5 percent of all radiographs. After removing 412 report-labelling errors, expert review found 31 clinically significant misses, an estimated 0.05 percent miss rate, mostly subtle or overlapping lesions. For comparison, a 2023 retrospective autonomous-reporting study found 7.8 percent of all radiographs (28 percent of normal PA films) could be reported autonomously with sensitivity above 99 percent, and a vendor case study at Leiden reported 15 to 20 percent autonomously reported at 99.9 percent sensitivity.
svg.title: Normal-CXR triage: the operating point
svg.text: Removing normals: what a 97%-sensitive CXR triage model actually does
UK silent trial, 5 NHS sites, 12 months (Radiology: AI 2026). Top three bars are to scale.

g.text: read by radiologists as usual; PPV 57%, so many are true normals
Sensitivity 97% · Specificity 35% · 412 NLP report-label errors removed before review
The model is tuned to almost never call an abnormal film normal, so it releases only the most
obviously normal ~1 in 5 films. Workload saved is bounded by specificity, not by accuracy.
• Retrospective multicentre (Radiology 2023): 7.8% of all films (28% of normal PA films) autonomously reportable, sensitivity >99%.
• Oxipit ChestLink (CE IIb autonomous; vendor case study, Leiden): 15–20% of studies auto-reported at 99.9% sensitivity.
Vendor figures are marketing claims, not independent evaluations. Settings, case mix and definitions of "significant miss" differ.
